div.head: I Ew 1.2
div.ab: Eac we cwædon: se ðe tyman scolde, þæt he hæfde ungeligene gewitnesse ðæs ðæt he hit on riht tymde, oððe þone að funde, ðe se gelyfan mihte ðe onsprece.
Eac we cwædon: se ðe tyman scolde, þæt he hæfde ungeligene gewitnesse ðæs þæt he hit on riht tymde, oððe ðone að funde, ðe se gelyfan mæge ðe onspræce.
Amplius diximus de illo, qui aduocare debet, ut habeat credibile testimonium de hoc, quod recte aduocat, uel iusiurandum inueniat, cui repetens credere debeat.
Eac we cwædon: se ðe tyman scolde, þæt he hæfde ungeligene gewitnesse ðæs ðæt he hit on riht tymde, oððe þone að funde, ðe se gelyfan mihte ðe onsprece.

Auch bestimmten wir: wer [im Anefang angegriffen] zur Gewähr zu ziehen im Begriffe steht, dass er wahrhaftes Zeugniss dafür habe, dass er das [angegriffene Werthstück] rechtmässig zur Gewähr zieht, oder solchen Eid erbringe, dem der Kläger glauben könne.

We also determined: whoever [having been challenged by attachment] is about to vouch to warranty, that he should have truthful witness that he is rightfully vouching [the attached item] to warranty, or produce such an oath as the plaintiff can believe.

Further, we have declared that he who has to vouch [another man] to warranty, shall have trustworthy witness that he is doing so in accordance with the law; or he shall produce an oath which he who brings the accusation may place confidence in.

note.seg: Die redenden ‘wir’ sind König und Witan. — Praeteritum hängt von cwædon ab; sculan hier Hilfsverb; s. Toller s. v. n. 12
The ‘we’ who speak are the king and the Witan. — The preterite depends on cwædon; sculan is here an auxiliary verb; see Toller s. v. n. 12
Vgl. Gl Anefang 12. 10a, wo Q Bürgschaft ändert in testimonium, vielleicht aus dieser Stelle
Cf. Gl Anefang 12. 10a, where Q changes surety to testimonium, perhaps on the basis of this passage
Ebd. 10. Der Eid geschieht also mit Helfern, wie 1, 3 Ende. Die Formel des Eides ist vielleicht Swer 3, 3
Ibid. 10. The oath is thus taken with helpers, as at the end of 1, 3. The formula of the oath is perhaps Swer 3, 3
Liebermann suggests that the form of the oath is perhaps given in The Formulæ for Oaths, cap. 3 § 3.
